current.title: Kids Are Being Diagnosed With ADHD Way More Than Before
current.hook: Your kid's odds of an ADHD diagnosis just hit 11.4 percent.
current.closing: More labels. Still not enough help.
current.question: Were you diagnosed as a kid? Tell me.

held_for: judge: A chart-first explainer: a bar chart, a timeline, two text percentages, two discs and a stock balance scale. Data points and dances beside them and never causes a number, and he covers the 53.6% label in the closing.
reasons: judge: A chart-first explainer: a bar chart, a timeline, two text percentages, two discs and a stock balance scale. Data points and dances beside them and never causes a number, and he covers the 53.6% label in the closing.

judge.one_line: A chart-first explainer: a bar chart, a timeline, two text percentages, two discs and a stock balance scale. Data points and dances beside them and never causes a number, and he covers the 53.6% label in the closing.
problems: The hook opens on a finished static bar chart that matches seg0 almost frame for frame, so about 3.6s carry one picture with nothing new arriving.
seg1 is a plain timeline chart; Data walks along the axis while the bars rise by themselves.
seg2 shows boys 15% vs girls 8% as text beside two identical mascots; nothing demonstrates the gap or the 'catching up' claim.
seg3 is two discs with numbers, a bare number card, and its white 53.6% is low contrast on the yellow fill.
seg4's balance scale barely tips for 53.6 vs 46.4 and does not show 'more labels, not enough help'; Data covers '53.6%' and 'Taking ADHD'.
Data is decorative in every scene: he points, raises his arms, dances or leans, with no setup, action or payoff tied to a number.
fixes: Hook: open on the shock as a subject shot, a classroom where 11 of every 100 desks carry a diagnosis tag, with Data stamping the last ones. Do not reuse the seg0 chart.
seg1: make the rise physical, for example Data stacking diagnosis folders into a pile that grows from 7.8 to 11.4 per 100, with the 2003 size ghosted on the pile.
seg2: make it a race or fill made of the subject, with boys' and girls' file stacks where the girls' stack closes the gap. Data does the stacking.
seg3: replace the discs with kids receiving pill bottles from Data and stop at 53.6%. Use dark ink on the accent fill, or put the number off the fill.
seg4: keep Data and every mark off the labels. If the scale stays, make it weigh labels (diagnoses) against help (treatment) so it tips hard.
Give Data one agent act per scene so his hands are on the moving part.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
